2026-11-25.title: Wednesday of the Thirty-fourth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: They sing the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb
Great and wonderful are all your works, Lord, mighty God!
By your endurance you will gain your souls
2026-11-25.alt: Optional memorial: St Catherine of Alexandria, virgin and martyr.
2026-11-25.verse: But not a hair of your head will perish. By your endurance you will gain your souls.
theo: Jesus does not promise his disciples an easy road. They will be arrested, handed over to synagogues and prisons, brought before kings and governors, even betrayed by family. But he turns it around: “This will give you an opportunity to testify.” He promises “words and a wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to withstand”, and a paradox: some will be put to death, yet “not a hair of your head will perish”. Ultimate safety is not physical survival but belonging to God.

Revelation shows the end of that endurance: the victors standing beside a sea of glass mixed with fire, holding harps, singing “the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb”. As Israel sang after crossing the Red Sea, the martyrs sing after passing through persecution. St Catherine of Alexandria, remembered today, is honoured in tradition as a young woman who defended the faith with wisdom before philosophers, a living sign of Luke 21:15.
outline: Ask: when has your faith cost you something?
Perseverance gains the soul; victory ends in song.
“Not a hair of your head will perish.”
live: When your faith is mocked today, answer with calm and kindness.
Keep one good resolution you are tempted to drop.
2026-11-25.prayer: Lord Jesus, when my faith is tested, give me words and wisdom, patience and courage. Keep me in your hand, so that by endurance I may gain my soul and sing the song of the Lamb. Amen.

quick: Persecution becomes an opportunity to testify.
Christ gives his witnesses words and wisdom.
By endurance we gain our souls.
2026-11-25.action: Answer mockery of your faith with calm kindness.
2026-11-25.question: Which good resolution am I tempted to drop?

homily: Dear friends, Jesus does not promise his disciples an easy road. They will be arrested and persecuted, handed over to synagogues and prisons, brought before kings and governors, even betrayed by parents, brothers and friends. But he turns it around: this will give you an opportunity to testify (Luke 21:12–13).

He promises words and a wisdom that none of their opponents will be able to withstand, and then a paradox: some of you will be put to death, yet not a hair of your head will perish. By your endurance you will gain your souls (Luke 21:16–19). Our final security is not survival, but belonging to God.

Revelation shows where this endurance ends: the conquerors stand beside a sea of glass mixed with fire, holding harps, and sing the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb (Revelation 15:2–3). As Israel sang after crossing the sea, the faithful sing after the trial.

Today the Church remembers St Catherine of Alexandria, honoured by tradition as a young woman who defended the faith with wisdom. When your faith is mocked, at school, at work or online, answer calmly and kindly. And keep one good resolution you are tempted to drop. Endurance wins the soul. Amen.
kids: Children, being a friend of Jesus is not always easy, but Jesus promises to give us the right words. If someone laughs at your faith, stay kind and brave!

intro: Persecution becomes testimony; Christ gives wisdom; endurance ends in the song of the Lamb.

sub: Every trial is a chance to witness.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.

But before all this occurs, they will arrest you and persecute you; they will hand you over to synagogues and prisons, and you will be brought before kings and governors because of my name. This will give you an opportunity to testify.
points.apply: Witness calmly when your faith is questioned.

sub: Moses feared he could not speak.
q: Now go, and I will be with your mouth and teach you what you are to speak.
For I will give you words and a wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to withstand or contradict.
points.apply: Learn one answer of the Catechism by heart.

sub: The victors sing after the trial.
q: The LORD is my strength and my might, and he has become my salvation; this is my God, and I will praise him, my father's God, and I will exalt him.
And they sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb: “Great and amazing are your deeds, Lord God the Almighty! Just and true are your ways, King of the nations!”
points.apply: Praise God today in the middle of a difficulty.

concl: Not a hair of your head will perish.
2026-11-25.resolve: Keep one good resolution steadily until Christmas.
